project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to purchase equipment to allow the hospital to provide cutting edge and efficient care to patients in the age of COVID-19 and possible future pandemics. Equipment purchases from this grant will include a clinical communication and collaboration platform, an upgraded phone system, portable diagnostic and treatment equipment, portable beds and stretchers, lifts, smart beds, and cutting-edge diagnostic and treatment technologies. Like many hospitals, Brattleboro Memorial had to shift gears during the pandemic, providing treatment and testing and later immunization for COVID, while having to shut down many elective procedures that often provide a steady source of revenue. They also needed to adapt to new ways of providing care, such as expanded telemedicine services and greater distancing. The hospital has developed a comprehensive plan to update equipment throughout the hospital with these concerns in mind. More technologically advanced equipment will support telemedicine and shorten time required for treatments, requiring less close contact without sacrificing interaction with patients. Additionally, acquiring more portable equipment and lifts to assist in moving patients and equipment will mean patients have to move around the hospital less, can be quickly isolated and still receive treatment in place, and can be moved and monitored with less physical contact from providers, reducing risk of infection for both patients and providers. The remainder of the project will be funded by applicant contribution.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to purchase equipment, including a pickup truck with a customized vacuum pump and lift gate, storage tanks, office and lab furniture, safety equipment to support the activities of Rich Earth Institute, Inc.s research facility in Brattleboro, Vermont. Rich Earth Institute is a groundbreaking non-profit that engages in research, education and technological innovation to advance the use of human waste as a resource and has recently been expanding their programs. Their unique work benefits the community in two important areas: improving water quality and supporting local farms. The Institute currently provides regular urine collection and recycling services to approximately 200 people throughout Windham County, representing approximately 95 households, and will soon include several public and business facilities that are installing urine diverting toilet fixtures. Their program keeps urine out of the wastewater stream, which reduces the amount of damaging nutrient pollution flowing into groundwater and surface waters. The urine is processed into a sanitized liquid fertilizer product, which is distributed to local farmers for growing hay. Over 10,000 gallons of urine is processed per year, providing four farms with fertilizer, and with recent grants five additional farmer partners will be added. Rich Earth Institute has also been able to expand their staff team and internship programs and has plans to build a new collection depot in Rockingham within the year. Although currently assisting local farmers, the long-term impacts of Rich Earth Institutes work may be far reaching for the agricultural sector as well as addressing pollution issues. The equipment they are able to purchase with this grant will help support the expanding role Rich Earth Institutes research facility in Brattleboro.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to establish a town-owned, centralized wastewater system for the town of Montgomery, Vermont. The town will construct a grinder pump collection and conveyance system and three separate septic tank and infiltration areas for treatment and discharge. This will include construction of roughly nine miles of pipe and will establish 165 connections, including residences and commercial properties. This project will address health and sanitary issues, as several existing private systems are either troubled or failing, and will also help to protect valuable environmental resources such as the Trout River. Current lack of wastewater capacity limits business and economic development in the town center, and negatively impacts residential property values. Additional funding for this project will come from a Northern Borders Regional Commission Grant and the states Clean Water Revolving Loan Fund.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to provide technical assistance and training to direct solid waste management programs to 19 communities in Washington, Orange, and Caledonia counties in Vermont. Central Vermont Solid Waste Management District will provide a series of educational events under its umbrella project, Protecting Ground Water Through Hands-On Education. This project combines development and implementation of a home assessment tool with hands-on workshops and trainings to educate the community about managing waste materials appropriately that, if handled improperly, contaminate waterways either by inappropriate flushing down drains, or as landfill leachate. The project includes a solid waste management home self-assessment tool, workshops on reducing use of hazardous and landfill-banned materials, food service industry seminar designed to teach commercial cooks strategies for reducing food waste, and a community fair featuring vendors and community partners to promote using non-hazardous products, water quality awareness, and waste reduction.
